title: How Dagobert Renouf grew Logology and 60k Twitter followers by connecting, not just posting
summary: Dagobert explains how a startup that failed on "build it and they will come" found its only working channel in Twitter. He covers the reply-first growth method, why authenticity beats AI-copied tweets, using memes to build trust, and why founders should market as a person rather than as a company.

principles.text: Building a good product is not enough; without eyes on it, nobody cares. Marketing has to be done from day one.
principles.quote: we realized if we're not putting eyes on this product nobody's gonna care like it's not enough

principles.text: When all else fails, go all in on one channel that shows traction. Twitter scaled linearly with followers for Logology.
principles.quote: we failed at everything else we tried marketing wise we don't really have any other options so let me just go all in on Twitter and see where it takes us

principles.text: With a tiny audience, spend your time connecting (replying to others) rather than tweeting into the void. Replies carry the same viral potential as tweets.
principles.quote: instead of spending your time tweeting you need to spend your time connecting

principles.text: Reply to accounts at your own level in your niche, about 30 minutes a day. That is usually enough to reach 500 to 1000 followers.
principles.quote: spend 30 minutes a day at the beginning just looking for people who inspire you in your Niche and connecting with them replying to their stuff

principles.text: Don't copy viral tweets or lean on AI-generated ones. Audience built on borrowed content doesn't care about you, so it won't buy from you. Care from followers matters more than follower count.
principles.quote: between two times more and ten times more it doesn't change much what matters is how many people care

principles.text: Market as a person, not a company. People follow founders, which builds trust, authority and opens PR, partnership and SEO opportunities.
principles.quote: you have to use it as a person and kind of build that personal brand of your thoughts your vision
